title: Violet’s Big Family
sub: PreK–Kindergarten · Home, family and the letters we keep
objective: Children will meet Violet Dina Want, a real woman born in London in 1907, through her family’s photographs and the story her family wrote down. They will hear how she helped at home, grew food, sewed, played the piano and loved roses; count the people in a family photograph; and learn that families keep letters and photographs to remember the people they love.

objectives.heading: By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
objectives.why: Every family has stories worth keeping. Letters and photographs help us remember the people we love.

items.screen: tell you something Violet did at home

materials: A letter or a card in an envelope, and a family photograph of your own if you like
The *Show your class* page (page 3), projected or printed
Crayons, including red or orange for the rose
questions: How many people can you count in this photograph? Can you find the baby?
How did Violet help her family when she was a girl?
What would you like to hear Violet play on her piano?
Why do families keep old letters and photographs?
Who would you write a letter to?
connection: **Visit the exhibition:** look at the family letters in the display case, from Violet’s estate. Count her photographs on poster 2: there are four.
**Virtual visit:** in *Violet’s Life*, open the little house, the piano and the rose, and look at the photograph at each stop.

steps.title: A letter, and a photograph
script: Hold up the envelope and take out the letter. *“Has anyone ever had a letter, or a card? Families keep letters and photographs for a long, long time.”* Then show the photograph of Violet, and wait before you say anything about her. *“This is Violet. She lived a long time ago. What do you notice about her?”* Take answers: her hat, her gloves, her long coat.

steps.purpose: Look before any story: wonder who she was.
students: What do you notice about her?

steps.title: A big family
script: Tell the story simply. *“Violet was born in 1907, more than a hundred years ago, in London, a big city in England. She had three sisters and two brothers. That is a big family! Violet helped look after her little sisters after school. Her father taught her to grow vegetables in the garden, because a garden gave the family food to eat.”*

steps.title: Music, sewing and roses
script: *“When Violet grew up, she married Harold. She said she chose him because he made her laugh. They had children of their own, and Violet was very good at sewing: she could take a grown-up’s coat apart and make it small enough for a child, so her children were always warm. Violet always had a piano. She played it by ear, without any music written down, and her family and friends came to sing and dance at lively parties. And when she had a garden of her own, she grew flowers. Her favorite flowers were roses.”*

steps.title: Letters to keep
script: *“Every March is Women’s History Month. We remember women who did great things, and women like Violet, too. Violet’s family wrote her story down, and they kept her old letters and photographs. Now they are in the Mini Museum, so we can remember her.”*

screen.text:
Violet’s family wrote her story down.
They kept her letters and photographs.

steps.purpose: Say why the letters and photographs are in the museum.
students: Why did her family keep them?

steps.title: Count the family
script: Show the family photograph on page 3. Count the people together, pointing to each one: five women and a baby, **six** in all. Let children find the baby in the white dress. *“This photograph is very old. Violet’s family kept it safe for a long time.”*

screen.caption: A family group outside a house

steps.purpose: Count the people in a real family photograph from long ago.
students: Count the people. Touch each one in the air.

steps.title: Your handout
script: Each child works on a handout. All three count the same family photograph and end with something for a letter of their own.

levels.name: Green Level
levels.summary: Picture-led. Count the people and circle the number, color Violet’s rose, follow the dots from Violet to her piano, trace *DEAR*.

levels.name: Yellow Level
levels.summary: A little writing. Count and circle, draw a line from Violet to her piano, copy *DEAR* under a model, then draw a picture for a letter.

levels.name: Red Level
levels.summary: Draw and tell. Count, find the baby, choose one of Violet’s things and tell why, then draw a letter to someone they love and start it *Dear…*

steps.purpose: Count, trace and draw, at the right level for each child.
students: Count the family. Then make something for a letter.

steps.title: Look back
script: Put the three questions on the screen. For each, children show a thumb up, sideways or down. Then say: *“Violet’s family kept her letters and photographs to remember her. Who in your family would you send a letter to? Tell a partner.”*
